Many portents causing destruction are seen here: Putana's death, the overturning of the cart,
brahmapuran:184:45	the falling of the two trees without wind or other cause. Therefore let us go from this place to Vrindavana without delay,
brahmapuran:184:46	before the evil of great earthly portents overwhelms Vraja. Having so resolved, all those dwellers of Vraja
said, "Let each go to his own family quickly; do not delay." Then in a moment they set out with carts and cattle wealth,
the Vraja-dwellers driving the herds and the calf-keepers in groups. In an instant the place of Vraja, shaken in all its parts,
became filled with crows and she-crows, Brahmins. Vrindavana, by the revered Krishna of untroubled deeds,
thought of with a good mind, wishing the increase of cows, then, though very dry, in the season of dharma, best of Brahmins,
became everywhere like the rainy season with fresh grass. Then all Vraja was settled in Vrindavana,
arranged in the shape of a half-moon bounded by carts and fences. Rama and Damodara then became calf-keeping boys.
Staying there, the two roamed the cow-pen with child's play, with peacock-feather crests, garlands of forest flowers,
making music with cowherds' flutes and leaf-instruments, with crow-wing locks, like two youthful fires.
Laughing and sporting they wandered through that great forest; sometimes laughing at one another, playing with others,
with the cowherds' sons they wandered tending calves. In passing time the two became seven years old,
the protectors of the whole world, calf-keepers in the great Vraja. Then came the rainy season, with the sky covered by masses of clouds,
making the directions as one with streams of rain, the earth rich with newly grown flowers, covered with red insects,
as if adorned with emerald and ruby. Rivers flowed on all sides, going off their courses,
like the minds of the ill-disciplined on getting new fortune; and the two mighty ones came to Vraja at will out of season and played with the equal cowherds like two immortals.
Seeing it, very terrible, like another mouth of death, the revered Madhusudana thought:

In this lives that wicked Kaliya, whose weapon is poison, who, conquered by me, abandoned his place and, wicked, fled into the ocean.
brahmapuran:185:7	By him this entire Yamuna, going to the sea, has been fouled; neither men nor cattle, tormented by thirst, enjoy it.
brahmapuran:185:8	So I must subdue this king of serpents, so that the dwellers of Vraja, constantly frightened, may roam in peace.
brahmapuran:185:9	For this I took this incarnation in the world of men: that those on the wrong path, the wicked, be punished.
brahmapuran:185:10	So, climbing this broad-branched kadamba tree not far away, I shall leap into this pool and destroy the poison-lord's life.
Thus reflecting, he tightly bound his girdle and then fell swiftly into the pool of the king of serpents.
By his falling, that great pool was agitated and sprinkled the trees growing even very far away.
Scorched and sprinkled by the water heated by the flames of the serpent's evil poison, those trees at once blazed, the edges of the directions filled with flames.
Then Krishna struck the Naga pool with his arms; and hearing that sound the king of serpents approached,
copper-red eyes from anger, with hoods full of flames of poison, surrounded by other greatly poisonous, red, wind-eating serpents.
Hundreds of Naga wives, adorned with lovely necklaces, with the beauty of their earrings moving as their trembling bodies shook,
then the serpents wrapped Krishna in their coils, and also bit Krishna with mouths made turbid by flames of poison.
Seeing him fallen there, crushed by the serpents' coils, the cowherds, coming to Vraja, cried out, sluggish with grief:
Krishna has gone, immersed in delusion, into Kaliya's pool; he is being eaten by the king of serpents. So come, do not delay.
Hearing these words like a thunderbolt-strike, the cowherds and cowherd women, led by Yashoda, went quickly to the pool.
Alas! Where is he? The people, the gopis greatly agitated, with Yashoda, wandered, running, stumbling.
Nanda the cowherd, the cowherds and Rama of wondrous prowess quickly went to the Yamuna, eager to see Krishna.
There they saw Krishna come under the power of the serpent king, made helpless, wrapped in the serpent's coils.
Nanda the cowherd became motionless, gazing intently at his son's face, and Yashoda, the fortunate, became so, best of sages.
The gopis, others weeping, saw him afflicted by grief, and with love, choked with fear, said to Keshava:

We shall all enter this great pool with Yashoda; it is not right for us to go to Vraja from the king of serpents.
brahmapuran:185:27	What is day without the sun, what night without the moon, what are cows without milk, what is Vraja without Krishna? Without this Krishna we shall not go to Gokula.
Hearing the gopis' words, the mighty son of Rohini, seeing the cowherds distressed, his eyes steady, said,
and seeing Nanda very downcast, his eyes fixed on his son's face, and Yashoda faint with swoon, to remind of Krishna's greatness:

God of gods, why is this human attitude shown by you? Do you not know yourself, why another?
brahmapuran:185:31	You are the navel of this world, the support of the gods, the maker, destroyer and protector, the three worlds, you consist of the three Vedas.
brahmapuran:185:32	Krishna, for the two of us who have descended here, the cowherds are the kin, and the cowherd women; why do you neglect your kin as they sink?
brahmapuran:185:33	The human state has been shown, a child's conduct has been shown; so let this wicked one, with fangs as weapons, be subdued, Krishna.
Thus reminded, Krishna, with lips parted in a smile, struck, and freed his body from the serpent's coils.
Bending the middle hood with both hands and mounting it, he danced, with great valour, on the heads that were bent.
Wounds appeared on the serpent's hood from Krishna's stamping feet; wherever it rose, his head bowed.
The Naga fainted, dizzy from Krishna's stampings, and vomited much blood by the fall of strikes of the staff.
Seeing him with head and neck crushed and blood flowing from his mouth, his wives took refuge in Madhusudana:

You are known, lord of gods, you are the supreme lord of all, the highest light, the inconceivable; the Supreme Lord is a portion of that.
brahmapuran:185:40	The gods are not able to praise him, the self-originating lord; how will a woman describe his true nature?
brahmapuran:185:41	Of whom the whole egg of the universe, made of earth, sky, water, fire and wind, is a small portion of a portion — how shall we praise him?
brahmapuran:185:42	So, lord of the world, show grace to this one who is sinking; this serpent gives up his life; let the gift of a husband be given as alms.
Thus addressed, consoled by them, the serpent, though weary in body, said slowly: "Be gracious, god of gods."

Lord, your eightfold natural lordship is supreme, unsurpassed; of him, what can I praise?
brahmapuran:185:45	You are higher, the first of the higher, you are the higher consisting of it; what indeed can I praise of him who is higher than the highest?
brahmapuran:185:46	As I was created by you, Lord, with birth, form and nature, so this was done by me.
brahmapuran:185:47	If I had acted otherwise, god of gods, then falling of the rod on me would be just, as your word is.
brahmapuran:185:48	Yet the punishment that the lord of the world has inflicted on me, I have borne; this punishment is a boon from you; let there be no other boon for me.
brahmapuran:185:49	Strength gone, poison gone, I am subdued by you, Achyuta; let one life be given; command me, what shall I do?

Serpent, you must not stay in the Yamuna water at any time; with your servants and family go to the sea water.
brahmapuran:185:51	And seeing my footprints on your head in the sea, Garuda, foe of serpents, will not strike you.
Having said so the revered Hari released the king of serpents; he bowed to Krishna and went to the ocean,
in the sight of all beings, with servants, children and kin, with all his wives, leaving his own pool.
When the serpent had gone, embracing Govinda as if come back from death, the cowherds sprinkled his head with water from their eyes.
Others, astonished, glad, praised Krishna of untroubled deeds, seeing the river's water auspicious.
Sung to by the gopis, with lovely deeds and conduct, praised by the cowherds, Krishna came to Vraja.
Then the cows, undisturbed, Brahmins, in that palm grove grazed happily on fresh grass, where it had been eaten before.
Then Krishna defeated Shridaman, and Rohini's son defeated Pralamba; others were defeated by Krishna's side cowherds.
They carried one another on their backs, going to the Bhandira trunk, and all those who were defeated there returned.
The Danava, quickly lifting Sankarshana on his shoulder, did not stop but went off, like a cloud with the moon.
Unable to bear him, the best of Danavas, in his fury, grew huge-bodied like a rain-cloud in the rains.
Sankarshana, seeing him, shaped like a burnt mountain, wearing garlands and long ornaments, with head grand with a crown,
terrible, with eyes like cart-wheels, making the earth tremble with his footfalls, being carried off, then said these words to Krishna:

Krishna, Krishna, I am being carried off by someone with a mountain-high form; see, a Daitya in the disguise of a cowherd.
brahmapuran:187:20	What is to be done by me now here, Madhusudana? Tell me; this wicked one is going in great haste.
Govinda, with lips parted in a smile, who knew the measure of the strength and valour of Rohini's son, said to Rama:

Why is this human attitude plainly adopted, Soul of all, secret of all secrets, by you, the secret self?
brahmapuran:187:23	Remember, lord of the entire world, cause, elder of the cause, yourself as one, and likewise how in the world and in the single ocean —
brahmapuran:187:24	you and I, universal Self, are one cause alone of this world; for the sake of the world we stand in difference.
brahmapuran:187:25	So remember, immeasurable one, your Self, kill the Danava; adopting this humanity, do good to your kin.
Thus reminded by the great-souled Krishna, Brahmins, the mighty Bala, laughing, crushed Pralamba.
He struck him on the head with his fist, his eyes red with anger; by that blow his eyes came out,
his brain was thrown out, and vomiting blood from his mouth the best of Daityas fell on the ground and died.
Seeing Pralamba killed by Bala of wondrous deeds, the delighted cowherds praised him, saying "Well done, well done."
Praised by the cowherds, Rama, the Daitya Pralamba having been felled, returned with Krishna to Gokula.
As Rama and Keshava thus played in Vraja, the rainy season passed and autumn came, with blooming lotuses.
When the time of clear sky and stars had come, they saw the dwellers of Vraja engaged in beginning Indra's festival.
Krishna, seeing the cowherds eager and longing for the festival, from curiosity, the greatly wise one said to the elders:
What is this festival of Shakra by which joy has come to you? Nanda the cowherd answered him as he asked with great respect:

Lord of clouds and waters is Shatakratu, king of gods, by whom the clouds, impelled, rain watery juice.
brahmapuran:187:36	The crops produced by that rain — we and other embodied beings live by them, enjoying them and gratifying the deities.
brahmapuran:187:37	These milch cows and cows with calves are content, nourished and satisfied by the crops grown by it.
brahmapuran:187:38	Land is not seen without crops, nor people unburdened by debt or tormented by hunger, where rain-bearing clouds are seen.
brahmapuran:187:39	The cloud takes this earthly water with the Sun's rays; Parjanya rains on earth for the welfare of all the world.
brahmapuran:187:40	Therefore in the rainy season all kings, glad, honour Shakra, lord of gods, in a festival, and we and other embodied beings.
Hearing thus Nanda's words about Shakra's worship, Damodara then said, for the anger of the lord of the thirty:

We are not farmers nor live by trade, father, and cows are our deity, since we are forest-dwellers.
brahmapuran:187:43	Logic, the Vedas, economics and statecraft are the four sciences; hear from me about economics here.
brahmapuran:187:44	Agriculture, trade and likewise the third, cattle-keeping: these are the sciences of economics, based on the three livelihoods.
brahmapuran:187:45	For farmers agriculture is the livelihood, for those living by trade, merchandise; for us, cows are the supreme livelihood; economics is by these three divisions.
brahmapuran:187:46	That science which a person is joined with is his great deity; that alone is worthy of worship and honour, and that alone benefits him.
brahmapuran:187:47	The man who eats the fruit of one and worships another gains no good here or hereafter, father.
brahmapuran:187:48	Let the renowned boundaries be worshipped, the forest at the border of the boundaries, and the mountains at the forest's end; that is our supreme goal.
brahmapuran:187:49	So let this mountain-sacrifice and cow-sacrifice be performed. What have we to do with Mahendra? Cows and mountains are our deities.
brahmapuran:187:50	Brahmins devote themselves to mantra-sacrifice, farmers to plough-sacrifice, and we, resting on mountain and forest, to mountain and cow sacrifice.
brahmapuran:187:51	So Mount Govardhana should be honoured and worshipped by you with various offerings, with the animal duly sacrificed.
brahmapuran:187:52	Let all the collections of the cowherd settlement be taken, without hesitation, and let Brahmins and other seekers be fed with them.
brahmapuran:187:53	When he has been worshipped, the fire-offering made and the twice-born fed, let the herds of cows go around with garlands of autumn flowers.
brahmapuran:187:54	This is my opinion, cowherds; if it is done with love, then love will be done to cows, the mountain and me.
Hearing his words, Nanda and the other Vraja-dwellers, their faces blooming with love, said, "Well done, well done," Brahmins.
Your opinion is excellent, dear, what you have said; I shall do all that; let the mountain-sacrifice be performed.
Thus the Vraja-dwellers performed the mountain-sacrifice and gave the mountain an offering of curd, rice-pudding, meat and the rest.
They fed Brahmins by hundreds and thousands; the cows, worshipped, went around the mountain.
The bulls bellowed like water-bearing clouds; on the mountain's head Govinda, in embodied form, said "I am the mountain."
He ate the many kinds of food brought by the best cowherds, Brahmins; Krishna in that very form,

with the cowherds, climbed the top of the mountain and worshipped, in his second body; when he had vanished, the cowherds, having received boons, performed the mountain festival and returned to their cow-pen.
Praised for his deeds by the delighted cowherds and cowherd women, their eyes wide with love, Krishna held up the mountain.
For seven nights the great clouds rained on Nanda's Gokula, clouds impelled by Indra, bringer of destruction to the cowherds.
Then, when the great mountain was held and Gokula protected, Indra, his vow made false, held back those clouds.
When the sky was cloudless, and Indra's design in vain, the cowherds came out of Gokula, glad, and returned to their place.
Krishna too then released the great mountain Govardhana to its place, seen by the Vraja-dwellers with amazed faces.
When Mount Govardhana had been held and Gokula protected, Indra wished to see Krishna.
Mounting the great elephant Airavata, the lord of the thirty, conquerer of foes, saw Krishna on Mount Govardhana,
tending the cows, of great valour, bearing a cowherd's form, the cowherd of the whole world, surrounded by cowherd boys.
And he saw Garuda, Brahmins, loftily gone invisible, making shade with his wings over Hari's head, the best of birds.
Descending from the king of elephants, Indra, in private, with a smile, his eyes wide with love, said to Madhusudana:

Krishna, Krishna, hear why I have come to you, mighty-armed one; this must not be thought otherwise by you.
brahmapuran:188:30	For the purpose of removing the earth's burden, you, the support of all, Supreme Lord, have descended to the earth.
brahmapuran:188:31	By me, hostile to the breaking of the festival, the great clouds that destroy Gokula were commanded, and this ruin was caused by them.
brahmapuran:188:32	The cows were saved from affliction by you, uprooting the great mountain; by that wondrous act of yours I am pleased, hero.
brahmapuran:188:33	I consider that the gods' purpose has been accomplished today, Krishna; this best of mountains was lifted by you with a single hand.
brahmapuran:188:34	Urged by the cows, Krishna, I have come here to you, because of you, for the cause of your cause, they being rescued by you greatly.
brahmapuran:188:35	Urged by the cows' word, I shall consecrate you; you will become Upendra, Indra of the cows, Govinda.
Then, taking a bell from the elephant Airavata that serves as his vehicle, he performed the consecration with water that purified.
While the consecration was being performed, at that moment the cows of Krishna made the earth wet with milk flowing from their udders.
Having consecrated Janardana at the cows' word, the lord of Shachi again said to Krishna with love and humility:

This was done at the cows' word; hear another thing from me, which I say, fortunate one, wishing to lighten the earth's burden:
brahmapuran:188:40	a portion of mine, a tiger among men, has descended on earth, called Arjuna; he is always to be protected by you.
brahmapuran:188:41	In removing the earth's burden that hero will make friendship with you; he is to be protected by you as yourself, Madhusudana.
brahmapuran:188:42	I know Partha born in the Bharata line from your portion; I shall protect him as long as I am on earth.

As long as I stay on earth, Shakra, subduer of foes, no one, lord of gods, will conquer Arjuna in battle.
brahmapuran:188:44	The great-armed Daitya Kamsa, another Arishta, Keshi, Kuvalayapida, Naraka and others —
brahmapuran:188:45	when they are killed, lord of gods, there will be a great war; know, thousand-eyed one, that there the lightening of the burden is accomplished.
brahmapuran:188:46	So go; you need not grieve on account of your son; no enemy of Arjuna will prevail before me.
brahmapuran:188:47	For Arjuna's sake, when the Bharata war is over, I shall give to Kunti all, led by Yudhishthira, unscathed.
Thus addressed, the king of gods embraced Janardana, mounted the elephant Airavata and went again to heaven.
Krishna too, with the cows and cowherds, came again to Vraja, by the path seen and purified by the gopis.
